## Evidence appendix — full instance tables, coverage audit, rejections

### Sample A — the 2026-08-20 session (NON-INDEPENDENT: one session, one protocol, one prompt naming the pattern)

**Clear non-fits (bucket B), as counter-evidence:** `fond-ulna-ball` (reducer cache key is

### Sample B(ii) — targeted hunt (~200 titles triaged, 41 read in full, **26 verified**, 15 rejected)

Spanning **2026-07-08 → 2026-08-19**, via unrelated discovery channels (live CI lanes, Gerrit review,
scheduled DC rehearsals, parity audits, extraction slices, operator escalations). Selection:

| triumphant-feline-drongo | `c9c6-a713-8bc6-4088` | `acli_cmd` honoured by `_verify_created_issue`; `update_priority` declares and never reads it |
| cardinal-secluded-avocet | `02cd-6c10-4ecf-49d6` | `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` defined/documented/env-resolved; never passed to `llm/runner.py` — every call rode the SDK default |
| clingy-kinetic-argusfish | `03b0-2290-f4f3-47a8` | Bedrock ids carry a colon; `_resolve_target`'s "already provider-qualified" test is `":" in model` → drops the configured provider for every `…-v1:0` id |
| frangible-applicable-snipe | `08c8-b6b2-4da6-4373` | deleted-source recovery routes through `rebuild_with_restore`; `_repair_ticket` still calls `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` directly |
| carnelian-planetary-silverfox | `b886-3c99-694b-4f91` | `CHECKBOX_NOTE` docstring says "**every** material-staleness reason"; the PRIMARY named-delta branch omits it |
| sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey | `573a-c8c2-ce2b-4b7f` | quarantine-and-retry recovery in `_store/sync.py`; `push_recovery._recover_dirty_merge` gives up with `merge --abort` (filed explicitly as "Parity sibling") |

| citric-preregal-ladybird | `751a-6a5c-1e08-46b3` | removing `rebar.llm.review_ticket` obliged retargeting 19 referencing test files; the 2 in `tests/external/` (**excluded from the `Verified` gate**) broke 4 live CI lanes |
| moldavite-evasive-elephant | `9590-34f5-21a8-41fc` | `c87afedba8` deliberately suppressed the `OK:` line; 2 live-DC cells still assert it — again gate-invisible |

Plus `accepted-androgenic-elk` (`0024-fa99-d5bb-49bc`): `_metric_invoke` omitted scc `--by-file` while

`abdominal-grieving-nandu`, `saintly-letterhigh-yaffle`, `rebel-vaporous-martin`,

### The copy-propagation variant (4 instances) — a DIFFERENT mechanism

| alias | id | what propagated |
|---|---|---|
| conscious-weighable-spittlebug | `3198-438c-72a5-470f` | missing `cwd=` on detached spawns: `57114212cf` (2026-06-12, `push.py`) → `9ad46965bd` (`enrich_drain.py`) → `d2dea317ec` (`compact_trigger.py`); all three fixed in `d575600381` |
| malevolent-emigratory-umbrette | `3a33-61e8-6e62-49a7` | an unlocked `git rm` + whole-index commit prune, "near-identical copy-paste" across 4 sidecars, bypassing `event_append.stage_and_commit` |
| chanceful-microbial-fallowdeer | `e63c-d987-6b99-4b56` | one terminal-state set copied into 4 drifted memberships, incl. phantom `done`/`completed` values absent from the status vocabulary |
| unrelative-inbred-piglet | `2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa` | a `_load_module` helper shared verbatim by 3 test files, producing two live `Mutation` classes |

Verified structurally: all three spawn sites lacked `cwd=` at `enrich_drain.py:319`, `push.py:209`,
`compact_trigger.py:206`, and `d575600381` touches exactly those three plus a new `_proc.py`.
**Why this defeats a producer-side criterion:** there was no contract change to trigger one, and the
reviewers of copies 2 and 3 had the strongest available correctness signal — the code matched existing,
shipped, working code. `/rebar-debug` Phase 2 Step 5's prior-art trust check
(`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:666-670`) only excludes code *"under an open bug or a
recent CI/test failure"*; `push.py` was under neither, so even that check would have passed.

### Coverage audit — what was enumerated and why each near-miss misses

49 plan-review criteria (`registry.load_criteria()`) and 14 code-review overlays
(`llm/code_review/registry.py`).

| mechanism | posture | why it misses this class |
|---|---|---|
| `omits_required_site` (grade) | **blocking**, 0.85 floor, HARD-OVERRIDE auto-high | a **grading axis**, not a hunter — it can only grade a finding another criterion produced |
| `T13` behavioral-prohibition consumer scan | advisory | triage (MIGRATED/EXEMPTED/**UNCOVERED**) + grep-reducibility fail-open is exactly right, but it triggers only on a **new prohibition**; every instance here is an **addition** |
| `code-review-deletion-impact` | **blocking@0.60**, content-triggered | the **subtractive** mirror (removed/renamed → dangling refs). No additive counterpart exists |
| `code-review-surface-parity` | **advisory, `blocking_enabled: false`**, globs `**/_commands/**`, `**/_lib_writes.py`, `**/_mcp_writes.py` | sibling set is a hardcoded triple; none of the actual missed siblings is one of the three |
| `project.symbol-reference-completeness` | advisory | requires a *named symbol* with an enumerated call-site list. `gates.py`, a help `.txt`, a latency budget, `xdist_group`, an ADR promise are not symbol references |
| `asserted-capability` | advisory | covers the **consumer-side** direction ("does module M provide C?"). The **producer-side** direction has no criterion |
| `G7` leaf-parent containment | blocking | leaf-vs-parent scope, not code siblings |
| `T12(c)` deploy ordering | advisory | producer/consumer *deploy order*, not site completeness |
| `project.portability` | **blocking@0.9** | breakage in an alternate client shape, not "did you update the other shape" |

**Empirical trigger check** (`registry.glob_triggered_overlays`): `surface-parity` glob-fires on
`9844f6de35`, `0f999860ad` and `d575600381` **today** and still would not flag them — the overlay fires
and is scoped out. It also shipped **2026-08-19**, after every Sample-A origin commit (`57114212cf`
2026-06-12, `9ad46965bd` 2026-07-09, `f943c7ef58` 2026-07-13, `746c1ba2e9` 2026-08-12, `d2dea317ec`
2026-08-13, `27b868ba55` 2026-08-14, `9844f6de35` 2026-08-15), so Sample A cannot indict it.
`T13` and `deletion-impact` both shipped 2026-07-06 and thus DID exist for most origins — they did not
fire because their triggers are *prohibition* and *deletion*.

### The debug-time protocol this would move earlier

`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:741-785` (Step 7 Axis 2) — shipped, version-controlled
project guidance, consumed downstream by `rebar-implement/SKILL.md:372-379`'s residual-gap disposition
sweep: **NAME THE RULE** (state the invariant as operation + property, *without naming the fixed
site* — "if you can only state it in terms of the file you fixed, you haven't found the rule yet") →
**CHANNEL CENSUS** over a fixed five-slot checklist (CLI / MCP-or-API / library facade / automated
callers / dual-direction) → **PER-SURFACE PROBE** citing `path:line` or marking **MISSING** →
**DISPOSITION** (fix now under RED→GREEN, or file + link `discovered_from`; "silence is not a
disposition"). Fully specified and proven — and it runs only *after* a bug exists.

### Method notes / limits

- Closed-bug corpus: **704**. Only **65 carry a `caused_by` edge** (<10%), so origin attribution is
  recorded almost exclusively where `/rebar-debug` traced it — the corpus cannot be mined
  exhaustively for "origin change that missed a site", and both samples inherit that bias.
- Sample B(i) was drawn with `random.seed(20260820)` over the 704-row closed-bug list; the classifier
  was given the definition but not Sample A.
- Both independent samples are *investigated* bugs, which favours bucket A (it needs three specific
  nameable things). The A rate in a corpus with weaker RCA records would likely be lower.

ANALYSIS (orchestrator-delegated critical evaluation):

## Premise validation — VALID, with three minor factual errors

Independently verified against the working tree, git history, and the ticket store (2026-08-21):

**Prior-art claims — all TRUE.** `docs/experiments/escaped-bug-review-gap-analysis.md` exists; line 66-67 is Class 3 with `halfwhite-chordal-stonefly` ("--class requirement added to CLI, not to MCP transition_ticket + NDJSON import — 9 prior PASS reviews"); that bug exists, closed `regression`, title matches. Lines 87-92 recommend exactly the three criteria named. `import-integrity` and `ci-gate-compat` appear NOWHERE in `src/` or `.rebar/` — never built (grep confirmed). `surface-parity` shipped narrower than the written recommendation: the rec says *content-triggered* + "require the MCP tool + NDJSON/import path be updated in lockstep"; the shipped overlay (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`) is GLOB-triggered on exactly `**/_commands/**`, `**/_lib_writes.py`, `**/_mcp_writes.py`, `default_posture: advisory`, `blocking_enabled: false`, and its prompt (`code-review-surface-parity.md:19-21`) confines siblings to the lib/CLI/MCP triple — no NDJSON/import channel. `deletion-impact` verified content-triggered, blocking@0.60.

**Coverage-gap claims — all TRUE.** T13's trigger is prohibition-only ("apply only when the plan NEWLY FORBIDS a previously-permitted action", `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md:322-325`). `omits_required_site` is a divergence *grade* on an axis, not a finder (guide lines 233, 243). Plan criteria count = 49 (confirmed via `registry.load_criteria()`). No criterion hunts additive-obligation misses; the residual-gap statement holds.

**Over-fire data — TRUE.** `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (¶ at ~line 263): 18,085 plan-v3 verified findings; the 1,307-finding omitted-scope-site class graded `none` ~90% (1,173); a blunt widening would have flipped 4.3% of runs PASS→BLOCK. The ticket cites its own strongest counter-evidence honestly.

**Commit claims — structurally TRUE.** `9844f6de35` touches `close_precheck.py` (+164) / `transition_close.py` (+29) and no `gates.py`, and updates BOTH `_commands/transition.py` and `_cli/help/transition.txt`. `0f999860ad` touches `_commands/transition.py` and NOT the help txt. `d575600381` touches exactly the three spawn files + new `_proc.py`. `57114212cf` is 2026-06-12. All three named commits glob-match surface-parity's `**/_commands/**` today, and the prompt's triple-scoping confirms it would still scope out the actual missed siblings.

**Spot-checked evidence tickets — all real, statuses match:** `kaolinite-head-wildebeest` closed `not_a_bug` (the rejection discipline is genuine), `citric-preregal-ladybird` closed `regression` (external tests / 4 CI lanes), `cardinal-secluded-avocet` closed (REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT), `chanceful-microbial-fallowdeer` closed `preexisting`.

**Errors found (none undermines the conclusion):**
1. "14 code-review overlays" — the registry has **15** `OVERLAY_IDS`.
2. `9844f6de35` is dated **2026-08-14** in git, not 2026-08-15 as listed.
3. "the *earlier* `9844f6de35` updated both help sources, proving the pair was maintained before it drifted" — chronology is BACKWARDS: `0f999860ad` (2026-07-19) predates `9844f6de35` (2026-08-14). The pair discipline was demonstrated *after* the drift, not before; the drift instance itself still stands.

**Currency:** concurrent ticket d890-e711 (`legalistic-combustive-nymph`, open) normalizes two criteria *synonyms* (sec/documentation) — orthogonal to this proposal; no conflict. The audit here reflects the current criteria set.

## Critical evaluation

**Cost.** Gate-economics (rebar metrics, last 30d): cost_per_accepted_change ≈ 70.2, first_pass_verification ≈ 0.79. Every added criterion runs on matching reviews; a blocking one adds false-block risk on top. The project's own 90%-`none` data predicts a broad additive-obligation criterion would be dominated by immaterial findings — the ticket correctly rejects the broad form. P0 costs nothing at review time (it is decision/doc hygiene). P1/P2 are edits to *existing* overlays, not new review passes. P3 is the only proposal that adds a new pass, and the ticket itself gates it on residue.

**Overlap.** Verified none: nearest mechanisms are a grader (`omits_required_site`), a wrong-trigger scan (T13, prohibitions), the subtractive mirror (`deletion-impact`), and a triple-scoped advisory (`surface-parity`). The gap is real.

**Enforcement mechanics.** P3's four-element anti-fire threshold ((a) cited added line, (b) path:line of a discharging site in the same diff, (c) path:line of a non-discharging site, (d) observable consequence) is concrete and mirrors `project.portability`'s pattern (verified: blocking@0.9 in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`). Caveat: "obligation" is inherently fuzzier than "deleted def" — deletion-impact earned blocking@0.60 on validity ≥0.95 for a *syntactic* trigger; an additive criterion should be expected to calibrate lower-precision, so advisory-first is right.

**Failure modes.** Legit deliberate phased rollouts (e.g. `airy-starchy-muntjac` explicitly scoped MCP out) would fire; the MIGRATED/EXEMPTED/UNCOVERED triage + the shipped surface-parity's "deliberately justified divergence must not fire" clause handle this if carried over. Test-only "missed sites" (the kaolinite class) are excluded by element (d). The definition-sensitivity the ticket admits (24%→60% base rate depending on strictness) means the prompt MUST encode the strict three-clause form or precision collapses.

## Recommendation: ADOPT-MODIFIED

Adopt **P0, P1, P2** now; make **P3 explicitly conditional** on measured residue after P1/P2 (the ticket already says "only if residue remains" — the modification is to make that a hard sequencing gate, not an option), and hold ALL postures at **advisory** until the AC's calibration replay (≥5 origin commits, hit/miss recorded) and FP-ledger measurement complete. Also correct the three factual errors above in any doc that inherits this evidence.

Three strongest reasons:
1. **The residual gap is verified, not asserted.** T13 prohibition-only, deletion-impact subtractive, surface-parity advisory + triple-scoped + glob-triggered, omits_required_site a grade — each checked in the working tree today. No mechanism asks "this change adds an obligation — enumerate the surfaces that owe it."
2. **P0/P1 are already-justified debt, not new policy.** The repo's own gap analysis recommended three criteria off 43 measured regressions; two were never built and the third shipped narrower than written, omitting the channel from its founding bug. Closing or formally declining documented recommendations is the cheapest real progress and requires no new evidence.
3. **The project's own calibration data bounds the risk.** The ~90%-`none` rate and the 4.3% PASS→BLOCK flip from blunt widening (18,085-finding corpus) are verified in docs/plan-review-gate.md — they simultaneously justify rejecting the broad criterion and demand the advisory-first, replay-gated posture for anything adopted.

## Operator decisions beyond adopt/reject
- P0 ruling direction: build `import-integrity`/`ci-gate-compat`, or write the decision-not-to into the gap-analysis doc (either satisfies the AC; someone must choose).
- Blocking promotion for widened surface-parity: requires the calibration replay — who runs it and against what corpus (real LLM spend).
- Whether P2's T13 lexicon widening (prohibition→obligation) risks diluting T13's current precision — a before/after replay on T13's own history would derisk it.
- Sequencing with d890-e711: none required (orthogonal), but both touch criteria docs — coordinate doc edits to avoid churn.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
P1 FP ASSESSMENT: would the recommended surface-parity widening (content-triggered on CLI arg/guard changes + NDJSON/import channel) have yielded historical false positives?

METHOD (judgment + git evidence, no LLM replays, per operator ruling). Modeled criterion: fires when a commit's diff changes CLI argument/guard surfaces under src/rebar/_cli/ (heuristic: git log -G over add_argument|required=|choices=|--flag tokens), channels = MCP (src/rebar/_mcp_*, mcp_server.py) + NDJSON/import (src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py, export_ndjson.py). Window: 85 commits qualify over the last 60 days; sampled the 40 most recent (2026-07-30 -> 2026-08-21), the ~40-commit cap binding first. Ground truth per commit from the diff plus subsequent history (follow-up fixes, escaped-bug tickets).

RESULTS — trigger count 40, split:
- TP-class 4/40 (10%): the MCP surface genuinely owed a matching update and the commit did not discharge it — d1466ff18f (transition --reason semantics), 63db6ac5a8 (--force-close -> --force rename), 0f34e8dc3b (reason-required dispositions: made compliant closes UNREACHABLE over MCP), d8fac8981b (unified --force[=<reason>] on transition+claim). All four are ONE defect family that escaped as bug 1128-505b ("MCP transition_ticket/claim_ticket lack reason/caused_by/ref/force parity"), fixed 2026-08-18 (e9969f8aec).
- Owed-and-discharged 8/40 (20%): parity updated in the same diff (32f2dd5f41, a22e6f3642, 710976dd2f, 694cf894de, ed0216f279, d21f2cb091, 31f352d535, 1fbfb5c691) — the criterion fires, verifies MIGRATED, emits nothing.
- Not-owed 28/40 (70%) = the FP-exposure pool: the trigger fires but no MCP/NDJSON obligation exists. Largest cluster: 6 RP-05 behavior-preserving parser/help-factory refactors (22efd71f10 alone rewrites 75 CLI files with zero semantic arg change). Plus 9 bridge/maintenance CLI-only verbs (fsck/doctor/tracker-maintenance/bridge pause/status/preview), guards living in shared core below all surfaces (ac3f6c1e60, e2bb6b3840), CLI-only UX (42cd70b889, d7d7594305), and — pointedly — 9844f6de35 (admin close dispositions), a named Sample-A origin commit: even the WIDENED channel list misses its real siblings (gates.py, a help .txt, spawn sites), while MCP/NDJSON owed nothing (close_class pass-through already threaded 2026-07-19).

Corroboration outside the sample: 662d8db31e (2026-07-18, persist bug-close --class) replays the founding bug halfwhite-chordal-stonefly — MCP+NDJSON threading landed a day later as 0f5dbc88b9 (376d); fb76631573 (--ref) also waited until e9969f8aec. The widened trigger would have been TP on both.

COMPARISON vs the ~90%-'none' precedent (docs/plan-review-gate.md, omitted-scope-site class: 1,307 findings, ~90% graded none): the genuine-obligation density here is 10% of triggers — the same order as that class's ~10% non-none rate. With perfect UNCOVERED-only discipline the criterion would emit 4 findings/40 triggers at 0% FP; at precedent-like discipline over the 70% not-owed pool it converges on the ~90%-none FP profile. Nothing in this sample suggests this criterion would beat the precedent.

DECISIVE POST-HOC FACT: every in-window TP belongs to a single class — write-parameter parity across library/CLI/MCP — which is now covered DETERMINISTICALLY: the bug-1128 fix (e9969f8aec, 2026-08-18) added the transport-agnostic write-parity oracle (tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py + test_write_parity_oracle.py): one contract table executed through all three adapters, PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED divergences fail the suite, known gaps are strict-xfails. The widened LLM criterion would have caught those 4 commits EARLIER, but going forward its entire demonstrated TP family is caught by CI at zero LLM cost. Residual uncovered channel: NDJSON/import is NOT one of the oracle's adapters; verified NDJSON-owing instances in the window: 1 (the founding --class bug).

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT the content-triggered widening. 70% of triggers owe nothing, the precedent predicts an FP-dominated criterion, and its only demonstrated TP family is now deterministically tested. The cheap deterministic residual (consistent with the operator's P0/P3 posture of preferring deterministic checks over LLM criteria): extend the write-parity contract with an NDJSON/import adapter or import-schema parity rows. If any change to the surface-parity criterion is made at all, the only evidence-supported subset is appending the NDJSON/import channel to the EXISTING glob trigger; converting the trigger to content-based is not supported.

## Context / Problem

Originally an evidence + proposal ticket for an additive-obligation parity criterion (P0-P3).
The operator rulings recorded in this ticket's comments (2026-08-21) narrowed the executable
scope, and this description now reflects only that approved scope:

- **P2 — APPROVED, no replay necessary:** widen plan-review overlay T13's trigger lexicon from

  the ci-gate-compat decline is being recorded in the gap-analysis doc under ticket 0778-b9c8.

The full original evidence (samples, base rates, prior art) is preserved verbatim in the first
comment on this ticket.

## Approach

**P2 (the code change).** T13's rubric body is the packaged prompt
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md` (trigger lexicon at lines 12-14 currently lists
prohibition verbs only: "block", "reject", "require … before", "enforce", "must pass",
"cannot merge until", "deny", "fail the build if"); its router applicability text is the
`"T13"` entry in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (line 1108, trigger: "plan
NEWLY FORBIDS a previously-permitted action"). Widen both from prohibition-only to obligation:
the overlay also applies when the plan ADDS a new obligation — a contract, invariant, schema
field, required argument, or a second site that must stay in step — that existing sites now
owe. Keep the MIGRATED/EXEMPTED/UNCOVERED classification, the fail-open abstain rule, and the
advisory posture/threshold unchanged. The deterministic pre-gate in
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_gate_rules.py` gains a second alternation branch carrying the
additive-obligation lexicon (per the Gerrit LLM-Review reachability finding on change 2035:
additive-only phrasings otherwise never reach the router); the audit-verbatim
enforcement branch (ticket 696a) stays byte-for-byte, and fires-side unit coverage is added. Regenerate
`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with its generator
(`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide`, implemented at
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_guide.py:48`) — never hand-edit the guide.

**P1 (analysis, no code).** Enumerate historical commits in a recent window (target: the last
~60 days or ~40 qualifying commits, whichever bounds first) that changed CLI argument/guard
surfaces under `src/rebar/_cli/` — i.e. commits the widened content-triggered surface-parity
would have TRIGGERED on. For each, determine ground truth from the diff and surrounding
history: did the MCP or NDJSON/import surface genuinely owe a matching update, and was it
updated? Classify each would-be finding TP/FP, report the FP rate, and compare against the
~90%-`none` omitted-scope-site precedent already cited in this ticket. Judgment + git
evidence only — no paid LLM review replays. Record the result as a ticket comment prefixed
"P1 FP ASSESSMENT:" with trigger count, TP/FP split, and an adopt/narrow/reject
recommendation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md` — widen title/trigger paragraph wording from
  prohibition-only to obligation
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `"T13"` trigger text and checklist

registry. Run those targeted tests plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`. Default: no new
tests — the edit adds no new runtime behavior (assume this unless an existing test fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] T13's rubric applies to newly ADDED obligations, not only prohibitions; checked by
